desert_p10_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_001.text: At dawn the chalk mark above the damp seam stood a finger-width from fresh moisture. Gao compared it with last night's sketch before letting anyone interpret the difference. The wet edge had advanced beneath the loading apron. A little clear water now gathered where dust had remained dry yesterday. The cistern gauge, farther north in its separate wall, held the expected lower line after their measured draw. Its cap was dry. Two nearby waters were behaving differently. Han watched Gao record them separately and understood why a single word, seep, would be too careless for the report.

desert_p10_002.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p10_002.text: The apron seam has changed. The roof store's outside fittings have not. We shall keep the source observations separate from the ground-water observation. Do not make the cistern guilty of every wet stone in its neighbourhood. The current road bend remains dry, according to the drivers' morning check. We can make our closing copy from the sound northern ledge, then depart. Du, bring the tracing. Yue, take the folding shade from your issued bag. Reflection may hide part of the north case now that the light has changed.

desert_p10_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_003.text: Tuo listened from her riding place beside the equipment cart. Her ankle was easier after sleep but still painful under full weight. Bao adjusted its support and asked the guide to keep the first stretch seated. The quiet driver checked the combined load against yesterday's arrangement. Water drawn from the tank had increased the margin; that did not excuse a loose cushion or unsecured box. Tuo said she now resembled a cherished instrument. The driver replied that instruments complained less and were occasionally willing to be covered. Tuo pulled the cloak over her knees, accepting half the comparison.

desert_p10_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_004.text: Han told the crew the closing group would return by the agreed time. Himself, Gao, Du, and Yue would make the last exterior look. The farrier stayed with the animals and the camp worker handled light packing under the drivers' help. Bao kept her treatment corner open until the tents were folded. Nobody loaded the loaned casks as if they still held water. Their emptiness changed the cart balance and made room for the riding arrangement. Yue fastened the field book inside its dry flap, put the spare pencil above it, and followed Gao toward the northern path.

desert_p10_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_005.text: The lower exchange looked darker under morning shadow. Its three openings faced a strip of pale ground that had once admitted freight. Drift softened the corners, making masonry seem like geology until an arch line caught the eye. Yue had begun to understand why travellers could walk past a known place and still fail to see how it worked. The visible parts invited familiar names. The hidden relations demanded time. They had spent enough to identify the station and its hazard. They had not bought the right to imagine every hidden room merely because its purpose pleased them.

desert_p10_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_006.text: At the service opening Gao set the folding shade to cut glare from the case pane. Du used the ordinary sighting glass from the sound ledge, adjusting it until the nearer column became clear. Yue copied his spoken readings in their separate rows. Han watched the time and the damp seam below, leaving the work to people who knew its method. A bead of moisture appeared on the outer glass, where cool air met the morning warmth. It blurred one heading. Gao waited for its path to clear instead of asking Du to supply the word he expected.

desert_p10_007.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_007.text: At the case opening Han held the shade's lower edge while Gao adjusted its angle. He had expected to spend the morning urging scholars away from paper. Instead he stood helping them see it. The cloth warmed quickly in his fingers. Through the pane Yue could make out the old clerk's ruled columns, some drawn straighter than the surviving type in Du's printed manual. A careful person had sat with these figures before any of the present crew was born. The thought made her want to copy everything.

desert_p10_008.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_008.text: Han's quiet question about the chosen rows brought the task back to its actual size. A small white plate beside the record reflected light from the window. Gao recognised it as a comparison surface for the old viewing arrangement, not another page. Its blankness had a purpose. Staff could judge changing light against it while reading the level strip and balance scale. Du admitted he had initially hoped the glimmer held an inscription. Yue found the ordinary explanation unexpectedly elegant. The engineers had left a place for seeing correctly, as deliberate as the places for writing.

desert_p10_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_009.text: She drew the plate in its position so a later visitor would not have to rediscover the distinction by disappointment.

desert_p10_010.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p10_010.text: The north opening keeps direct sun off the case for most of the day. That reduces heating and glare; the reflected plate gives staff a steadier surface beside the scales. We cannot judge the whole mechanism through this view. We can identify how the reading place was arranged. Put the opening's direction in the plan. A printer may think that small arrow expendable. It belongs to the evidence. If somebody compares a future observation made through an east window at noon, the conditions will differ before the numbers do.

desert_p10_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_011.text: Yue added the arrow carefully. It pointed toward the valley beyond the dark ridge, a place the present caravan had not entered. From this ledge she could see only a notch and a pale line of distant ground. The old staff had looked that way each morning, measuring conditions carried from beyond their own walls. Their work was local without being isolated. The roof catchment, weighing apron, and buried channel belonged to a larger terrain. She had begun the journey wanting to see the desert. Now she could see how much remained outside any one useful view.

desert_p10_012.speaker: du_she
desert_p10_012.text: The heading is summer checks, not winter returns. I can see the first two characters now. Leave the uncertain third as a blank until the pane clears again. This is why we needed the column boundaries preserved yesterday. The weather signs use the same shapes, but they sit beside another season's figures. If I had moved the row while summarising, I could have made the record claim something far more dramatic than its keeper wrote. Han, I need ten minutes for this nearest set, not an hour for everything beyond it.

desert_p10_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_013.text: Han granted ten minutes and made the start plain. The limit sharpened Du's choice. He copied the accessible heading, two complete rows, and the exact relation between the load symbol and level marks. He left the darker farther section untouched. Yue used the spare pencil when her first point wore too short to make clean figures. A new pencil line seemed almost luxurious after the worn one. She remembered Gao's advice about not forcing a reading to become encouraging. A clean blank was better than a handsome invented number, even when departure made the blank feel expensive.

desert_p10_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_014.text: The summer rows recorded limits after unusual rain beyond the northern ridge. The upper public approach reopened before the lower loading apron, which stayed closed pending foundation examination. A copied office reference named an inspection register held elsewhere. Du read it twice, then admitted he remembered that register's filing code from the records office. He had not recalled the summer restriction when the subscribers first sent their sketch. Gao wrote his present recollection beside the transcription, keeping memory distinct from the visible text.

desert_p10_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_015.text: The old record now offered another source to seek, without pretending the closed register stood behind the same pane. Du paused over a figure whose lower loop disappeared behind a water bead. He thought it might be eighteen; Yue's first impression was thirteen. Gao asked them to describe the visible strokes without naming the number. That made both readings less confident. They waited until the bead moved and found the second loop intact. Eighteen belonged in the chosen row. The dispute had cost less than a minute, yet Yue could feel the alternative account they had almost made.

desert_p10_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_016.text: She wrote the observation cleanly and did not preserve thirteen merely to advertise that she had participated.

desert_p10_017.speaker: du_she
desert_p10_017.text: I am grateful you disagreed before copying my guess. It would have looked very authoritative in your neat hand. Clerks can make uncertainty respectable by writing it well, which is one reason I try to keep them beside the person taking the observation. We shall include this row because the figure is visible now. The next row still has its lower half hidden. Leave that one. If the archive later supplies a fuller copy, it can answer our blank without needing to explain why two tired surveyors invented a beautiful number at the north window.

desert_p10_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_018.text: Han asked whether the disputed figure represented weight, level, or a count of days. Du pointed to the column heading and its relation to the adjoining symbol. It was a level measure, paired with a load restriction elsewhere in the same entry. Han had been ready to read it as a wagon count. The correction made him stop imagining a crowd of eighteen carts beneath the roof. Yue watched the scene become smaller and more exact in his face. A number could remain perfectly copied while being used for the wrong thing.

desert_p10_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_019.text: The report needed enough structure to prevent that cheaper kind of error too. Gao had Yue draw the heading and symbol beside the transcription rather than copying figures alone. The little facsimile would help readers compare their account with the later original. Du supported the page against the outside stone, keeping it clear of the case. Wind lifted one corner. Han steadied it with his free hand, shade still held in the other. For a moment the four looked like people assembling a kite with excessive seriousness. Yue nearly laughed, then saw Du smiling over the glass.

desert_p10_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_020.text: The work could remain careful while its appearance belonged to ordinary comedy. A line below the summer entry named maintenance of the northern lip after a heavy-rain season. Du read it as repair, then corrected the word to raised. The difference mattered: the workers altered the barrier height rather than merely restoring its old condition. Gao compared the inscription with the roof channel they inspected yesterday. A later modification could explain why the surviving stone lip differed from the standard plan. The record's word fitted a visible feature.

desert_p10_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_021.text: Neither alone proved every part of the source history, but together they strengthened the account they would ask the next team to examine. Yue saw where the old page's edge had darkened beneath its protective frame. It looked fragile enough that a careless attempt to retrieve it might destroy the evidence people wanted. Du said the next commission should include someone who handled old paper regularly, not merely a scholar pleased to meet it. He had restored minor sheets in his office but knew the case might hold damp seals and brittle bindings beyond that experience.

desert_p10_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_022.text: Han asked whether such a person lived in Bitter Wells. Du knew where to enquire. The name of a trade became more useful than another expression of reverence for history. Yue asked whether the summer rainfall meant the present damp seam came from a storm. Gao said it made the channel's seasonal label less reassuring, but did not identify today's source. Quarry drainage had changed south of them. High cloud stood north. The two possibilities needed present evidence. Their report could recommend keeping loaded carts off the apron and inspecting the channel without deciding which distant event owned every bead.

desert_p10_023.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_023.text: Han nodded. The subscribers wanted a route answer; that answer could be stronger than a complete theory. They had already seen enough to reject the proposed heavy loading ground. Gao looked through the opening once more at the brass linkage. Its upper arm disappeared under the loading floor; the lower scale stood beside the case. Freight weighed above could be read from the sheltered service room below. The system explained the apron as a working roof, not merely a broad place that happened to admit carts. She drew the visible linkage without claiming the hidden joints survived.

desert_p10_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_024.text: Han's intended reopening would require a structural and mechanical inspection. Yue watched him revise the project's cost in his mind. An ancient convenient ground had become a machine that needed ordinary skilled people.

desert_p10_025.speaker: han_xun
desert_p10_025.text: I should have asked whether the loading ground was ground before offering to price its reopening. That sentence will annoy me for years. We can use it at the meeting if necessary, though I hope someone kinder supplies the wording. The subscribers wanted shelter, a level place for transfer, and water along a shorter route. They may still obtain some of those things elsewhere. We owe them the distinction between what stands here and what they wish stood here. I can defend a report that disappoints them if it gives them a project they can actually choose.

desert_p10_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_026.text: Du offered to use more elegant wording, then admitted the plain sentence was stronger. Gao kept it in the rough meeting note. Yue thought Han disliked looking foolish less than he disliked leaving a practical question unanswered. That preference had saved the first driver from blame over the broken brake. Here it would cost him an attractive freight proposal. He did not welcome the cost. He stayed at the opening anyway, helping the copied row dry before it entered the case. The small action made his earlier speech believable without requiring anyone to declare him a virtuous man.

desert_p10_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_027.text: The final minute belonged to the source reference. Du read its filing code slowly while Yue copied each part. One character resembled the wind station's district name but carried an extra stroke. He did not omit it to make the reference familiar. Gao had him point through the sighting glass again, then agreed. They would ask the receiving office for that exact register, with a photograph or full transcript if one could be arranged by its own staff. No one promised the archive's answer.

desert_p10_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_028.text: The useful thing they could bring home was a question precise enough that a clerk might find it. Du copied the reference code, then set his pencil down at the agreed time. Han seemed ready to allow another minute, but the scholar did not ask. He had finished the chosen task. Through the north opening the case held further pages, glass surfaces, and a brass linkage shaped for the old balance mechanism. They remained where they were. Yue felt the temptation to call that leaving unfinished work, then remembered the half she had watched him finish carefully.

desert_p10_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_029.text: A task could be complete at its honest boundary while a building still contained unanswered questions. Gao took one final bearing between the north opening, the paired cairns, and the public ridge. The case location would matter to a later inspection team, which should not have to discover the safe viewpoint through another fall. Han signed the limited exterior observation with her. Du supplied the source-copy note and his records-office disclosure. Yue checked the drawing's turning point. No one signed that the buried hall was safe to enter.

desert_p10_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_030.text: The report would bring a specific place back to town, where people could fund the next work instead of demanding that curiosity substitute for its equipment. Beside the cistern outlet, they fixed a temporary notice to the old exterior bracket using a cord from the field bundle. It gave the date, estimated raw remainder, treatment need, foot access, and unsuitable loading apron in large writing. The cap stayed closed. Du used the local names beside the formal labels.

desert_p10_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_031.text: Han wanted the warning durable enough for the next carrier; Gao said the receiving house should arrange a proper board after reviewing the report. Their paper was a current message, not permanent infrastructure. Yue weighed its lower edge with a small dry stick so wind would not hide the essential lines immediately. The notice looked humble against the carved emergency inscription. It might fade, tear, or be ignored. That did not make writing it pointless.

desert_p10_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_032.text: Yue imagined the two rescued guides seeing the approach before they followed the shelf, and tried not to let that image turn into a promise that better paper could have solved everything. Their injury had required people, a stretcher, a clinician, and time. The new sheet supplied one piece of future help. She checked that the northern turn remained visible in the sketch, then stepped back with the others. On the return path Yue asked why the case records had been left at all.

desert_p10_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_033.text: Du thought closure had moved the annual summaries while local working material remained for a possible reopening. Some officials expected the northern traffic to return. Then another road attracted carriers, staff dispersed, and the old station lost its ordinary place in accounts. The case survived because its housing protected it, not because someone arranged a perfect treasure for future scholars. The explanation disappointed part of Yue that still wanted deliberate hidden wisdom. It pleased another part that understood neglect could preserve things as accidentally as it destroyed them.

desert_p10_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_034.text: Returning to Crescent House, Gao paused at the high point where both stations could be seen. The wind building's broad arch stood apart from the lower exchange's three openings. Their relation now seemed impossible to confuse, though it had been easy before arrival. Du said that feeling would be dangerous when he returned to the printer. The customer seeing a flat sheet would not have walked their northern ledge. Gao agreed. The figure needed to teach the difference to someone without their experience. Yue added the roofline thumbnail beside each name, giving the reader more than one route to recognition.

desert_p10_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_035.text: Gao stopped at the high viewpoint to redraw the roofline thumbnail. Her first sketch had made the lower exchange's middle opening too tall. Yue noticed the difference but hesitated to say it. The surveyor saw the hesitation and handed over the pencil. Yue adjusted the line, then checked it against the building rather than Gao's expression. The correction held. Gao accepted it without a lesson, which made the moment less memorable and more comfortable. Du watched with amusement. He said former pupils always learned to enjoy that particular silence. Gao told him he would have found hers worth cultivating earlier.

desert_p10_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_036.text: The north-facing window of Crescent House showed the little bird returning with another dry stem. Its nest-glass flashed briefly as the wind moved the material. Yue could now recognise the source from farther away because she had seen it clearly once. She did not mistake recognition for a new measurement. The bird vanished behind the sill, leaving the bright shard alone. Gao said the nest should appear as an obstruction on the exterior record but need no removal for the present report. The station's living tenant would retain its home while the old freight plan sought another roof.

desert_p10_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_037.text: At camp the drivers had packed nearly everything except the breakfast pot and treatment shade. Bao checked Tuo's foot once more and handed the guide her own staff for use at stops. Its place was within reach, not tied among distant rods. The camp worker's wrist could now manage ordinary light tasks without pain, though heavy striking remained deferred. Han read the revised accounts aloud to the workers concerned, including the extra cask carrying. The quiet driver kept her copy. An expedition ended its camp through objects and obligations, both easier to lose when everyone wanted the road.

desert_p10_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_038.text: At breakfast the camp worker asked whether the old service rooms used the same stakes and knots they carried. Du said records mentioned ropes but not their precise tying. The worker looked disappointed, then showed a shelter knot he learned from his grandmother. It released under a particular pull yet held when wind loaded the line sideways. Gao drew it in her private book because it might improve the next camp's arrangement. Knowledge had arrived from a restricted wrist at the edge of the table, without a licence or an ancient inscription making it important first.

desert_p10_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_039.text: Yue liked that exchange more than several grand discoveries she had imagined. The worker's grandmother had tied fishing nets before moving west after a flood. He rarely told the story because people immediately asked whether the flood was the reason he worked on dry roads. It was partly true, and too simple. He liked travel, disliked fish cleaning, and earned better on seasonal caravans than at the small town workshop. A life could contain a disaster without being explained entirely by it. Bao said she wished more patients remembered that when describing every present ache through one childhood injury.

desert_p10_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_040.text: Tuo looked at her ankle and warned the clinician against becoming too pleased with the analogy. Long Legs brought the repaired shade tape to Han for the next outfitter order. He had measured the failed tie rather than simply requesting a stronger one. Han copied the width and material, then gave the sample back. The driver said his mother would be astonished to hear he had provided specifications before a complaint. Han promised to phrase the letter so astonishment did not become a family emergency.

desert_p10_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_041.text: Their exchange sounded light, but Yue could see tomorrow's safer shade in the little torn strip. Good future work sometimes began with carrying an unglamorous failure home instead of hiding it under a better story. Bao wrote the water-screening case's remaining supplies on her replenishment list. She had enough for an ordinary return emergency but would need fresh complete sets before another abandoned-source assessment. Han asked whether the next commission should pay for them. She said yes, and for clean collection vessels kept apart from the crew's cooking pots.

desert_p10_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_042.text: The cask loan had helped this time, but a properly planned inspection should not depend on a keeper having spare capacity when they happened to arrive. Gao added the requirements to her next-work proposal. Their success was becoming a way to identify better preparation, not a reason to assume it again. Yue checked her own small inventory before the carts moved. The borrowed staff and flags remained Gao's; her habitual notebook, sword, practice lead, and fish stone belonged with her pack. One pencil was nearly spent, the other still serviceable. The issue cloak needed washing when they returned.

desert_p10_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_043.text: Nothing in the ruin had secretly entered the bag. She had gained observations, a few new tasks she could perform, and a clearer sense of the crew. Those were less easy to count than equipment. She could still name their sources, which mattered when memory later tried to make the journey more solitary than it had been. Tuo asked the quiet driver to stop boasting about the smooth ride before they reached actual rough ground. The driver said she had made no boast.

desert_p10_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_044.text: The guide admitted the compliment might have been imaginary because she wanted an argument small enough to win. Bao adjusted the cushion and told her to save arguments for the village tile players. Tuo said she still owed them a broken shoe story. The laughter moved around the cart while its brake remained set. Yue saw the guide testing the edges of her ordinary self again, making room for pain without letting it govern every conversation. The cook served a breakfast thicker than supper's broth.

desert_p10_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_045.text: He wanted the crew to begin the return with food in them rather than hope in a bag. Yue ate sitting against a cart wheel that had not yet been released. Plum lowered her muzzle toward the bowl and received a firm refusal from her driver before any theft became amusing. The mule returned to its measured feed. Du watched the scene and said his next edition should include a symbol for meals defended from livestock. Tuo replied that the symbol would occupy more paper than his entire northern route.

desert_p10_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_046.text: Gao gave Han the final provisional packet and retained the original field pages. Public copies held route facts, source labels, and current hazards; patient details stayed in the private rescue record. The separation mattered more now that the return would deliver both to offices capable of gossip. Han would present the full account to the cooperative and receiving house, with the collective's drainage evidence alongside it. Du would send his map corrections to the rival compiler as questions and observed changes, not a victory announcement. Yue had a smaller destination: a fish stone for the shoemaker's daughter.

desert_p10_047.speaker: han_xun
desert_p10_047.text: We go by the ridge to the quarry, return the casks, and take the inspected detour if the eastern culvert still carries water. Tuo may ride; drivers will rotate the leading turns as planned. We stop before fatigue turns a small trouble into an impressive one. The report is good enough to bring home. The next work will be better if we bring its people home too. I have said that often. You may laugh at me after the first mile, provided somebody remembers to look at the wheels while doing it.

desert_p10_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_048.text: Long Legs promised to reserve the laugh until a straight stretch. The quiet driver released the equipment cart's brake only after Bao settled Tuo's supported foot. Yue took her place where the last cart could see the red flag. The first pair leaned into their harness, and the caravan began moving out of the forecourt. Crescent House's song rose briefly behind them. Nobody answered it with the wooden bird this time. The driver had put the toy away for travel.

desert_p10_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_049.text: The unfinished duet could wait for another camp, which was a different kind of trust than believing a ruin remembered every visitor. At the ridge turn Yue looked back once. Their sleeping places showed only darker gravel and flattened dust. The stove waste pit had been covered; the hollow boundary cord remained because the hazard remained, marked for later travellers. Gao had left its purpose in the report rather than claiming the crew repaired the apron. The house's north window caught light around its bird nest.

desert_p10_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_050.text: Beyond it the lower exchange disappeared behind the rise, keeping its case and raw reserve. They had taken observations and measured water, while the place retained far more than the word found could contain. The first return descent was slow with Tuo riding. The equipment driver felt each hollow through the reins and cart frame, choosing the firmer wheel line before committing. Bao walked beside the cart on the roughest section, watching the guide's face rather than asking every minute whether she hurt. Yue carried the light staff behind them. Her own feet were tired but sound.

desert_p10_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_051.text: The new stage had not removed the need to watch a wheel path; it had made her more willing to accept that skill remained specific. Gao walked ahead with a field book full of things they had learned by staying ordinary. Near the black outcrop, Du stopped to correct one last local direction in the rough copy. He had drawn the path bending east too early. Yue saw it now because she had just walked the bend again. He made the change without complaint.

desert_p10_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_052.text: A map could become more accurate on departure than arrival, if its maker kept looking instead of treating the journey home as an empty repeat. Han waited while the pencil moved. The pause cost less than a mistaken line would cost a stranger later. Tuo called the correct turning point from her cart, pleased to contribute without dismounting. They passed the western cairn first, then the eastern marker farther below. From the wheel road the pair merged briefly in perspective, explaining why so many accounts called them one split monument. Gao asked Yue to note the viewing point.

desert_p10_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_053.text: Their correction could respect the old name while showing the source of its confusion. Du seemed almost cheerful about being wrong in an understandable way. Tuo said he would eventually make a lecture of it. He promised to keep the lecture shorter than the road. Han said he would accept that bargain only if its distance was measured from the same origin. The ridge opened into a long straight stretch. Long Legs delivered his promised laugh at Han's departure speech, then checked the first tank's underside as they halted. Its joints were dry.

desert_p10_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_054.text: The second driver checked his own frame; the equipment driver did the same while Bao eased Tuo's foot. The routine took several minutes and caught nothing new. Yue had once thought a check that found no trouble might be an unnecessary delay. Now she watched people use the pause to drink, adjust a strap, and exchange a useful word. The check had made room for more than a leak. At the first return rest Gao showed Yue how the reflected light changed the ridge's colour.

desert_p10_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_055.text: The same dark stone looked grey beneath a thin cloud and almost black when the sun returned. Survey sketches could identify shape more safely than relying on colour words alone. Yue added the outcrop's angular profile beside its label. She did not erase black, the familiar local description; she gave it a companion that survived the light. The little drawing improved the turning instruction. It also made her notice a low crack she had missed before, running away from the wheel path into harmless open gravel.

desert_p10_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_056.text: The farrier inspected that crack from the road's sound edge and found no change under the chosen wheel line. He reported the observation without promising what next season would do. Han kept the team moving after the rest. Yue felt a growing ease in hearing a bounded answer. Earlier she had wanted certainty to arrive in one complete sentence. On the road, useful confidence came through people naming the part they had checked. Her own fifth-stage examination had required the same habit across recovered trials.

desert_p10_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_057.text: The similarity did not make stones into meridians; it made her less impatient with honest limits. Gao asked Du whether he would revise the travel essay as well as the public sheet. He said the house could keep its song but lose its impossible memory. The new version would describe the shafts and the people who built them. It might sell fewer copies. He looked unpleased about that possibility, then said readers who wanted ancestors could bring their own. Tuo approved the line until he reached for a pencil.

desert_p10_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_058.text: She told him not to turn every spontaneous decent sentence into property. He laughed and let the phrase remain, for the moment, part of their walk. Du gave Gao his revised travel-essay opening while they walked the straight stretch. It named the wind station's builders before the sound. She listened, said the second sentence still made air into a keeper of ancestral memory, and returned the page. He groaned. Tuo offered to edit the whole essay with a blunt stick. Han said that method could lower printing costs dramatically.

desert_p10_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_059.text: Yue laughed until Du held up the page and pointed out that ridicule had not supplied a better sentence. Gao suggested the physical detail of the shaded outlet. He wrote it, muttering, and the piece began improving. The driver with the wooden bird asked whether a travel essay could include a child learning the wrong tune. Du said it could, if the child and parent agreed and the account did not make them foolish for the writer's advantage. The driver looked pleased by the answer and decided his daughter would insist on correcting every note.

desert_p10_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_060.text: Tuo said that sounded like an excellent editor. Yue heard the discussion while watching the last cart's sightline. Stories could travel with maps, each capable of helping people imagine a place and each capable of taking more than its author had earned. The cook rode beside the food bags, counting meals remaining after the bought contingency stock. They had enough for the planned return with a reserve, including the rider's bowl yesterday. He showed Han the total before settling the sack covers. The extra purchase had been ordinary expense, yet without it the source inspection would have meant stretching portions.

desert_p10_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_061.text: Yue liked the meal count's physical clarity: sacks, cups, and people she could see. It was a form of confidence different from pretending no delay would occur. The cook closed the book and offered her a small piece of dried pear. They stopped in a ridge shadow before the day's light grew harsh. Tuo remained seated while Bao examined whether the ride increased swelling. It had not noticeably worsened, though the guide needed the foot supported through the next stretch too. The others drank from the actual day's allocation, with more available when work required.

desert_p10_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_062.text: Han's water page began its new column at one thousand and sixty-one litres. The return would draw from that measured remainder. The raw cistern reserve belonged behind them, unable to become a comforting addition each time somebody spoke its name. Yue took the folded roof-water note out only to check the copy was dry. A little charcoal smudge from the treatment table crossed its blank corner, not the numbers. She left it there. The sheet's useful words had travelled through smoke, wind, hands, and a glass pane that sometimes refused to cooperate.

desert_p10_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_063.text: A fair copy would remove the smudge, which was sensible. She would keep the original as evidence of what they actually saw and wrote, not because disorder made it automatically true. Gao placed it back in the dry case beside the source diagram and actual batch record. The driver with the wooden bird asked Tuo whether the public ridge had ever carried the name Stone Channel. She said some carriers used the old name for the whole district, which helped neither geography nor argument. His grandmother called every western road the salt road regardless of destination.

desert_p10_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_064.text: Du said families could afford broader names than printers. The driver replied that printers ought to visit grandmothers before announcing which names people used. Yue laughed at Du's expression. The argument was light, but it pointed toward the task awaiting them in town: make a shared sheet without erasing the people whose ground it described. When the ridge wind eased, the crew walked for a while without talking. The mules' steps and the wheel rims supplied enough rhythm. Yue could feel her trained lower routes at rest beneath ordinary movement, distinct and quiet.

desert_p10_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_065.text: She did not open them to make the miles disappear. Their earned control remained available for a suitable task; walking still belonged to feet, breath, food, and rests. She found that steadiness reassuring. A stage could remain stable without demanding a demonstration each hour. Ahead, Bao offered the guide a drink and waited while she took it slowly over the cart's sway. At the next broad shoulder Han compared the travel pace with Tuo's seated estimate. They were making ordinary progress despite the careful descent.

desert_p10_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_066.text: No need to punish the crew with a longer hot stretch merely because yesterday's work had used an extra day. The food and water margins already included the actual schedule. He asked Gao when she wanted the next observation stop. She said the quarry approach itself would be enough unless they saw a change. Han visibly enjoyed an answer that did not generate another table. Du accused him of hating scholarship only until it saved freight. Han admitted freight often paid his affections.

desert_p10_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_067.text: He also said the source note had helped him understand the old map conflict, which was worth more than he expected from a paragraph. Du accepted the mixed compliment. Yue wondered whether people could improve their tastes the way they improved a cart brake, by noticing where a useful mechanism had been doing work unseen. The thought was too tidy for her private book, so she let it pass. The next turn required her eyes. She moved behind the last cart until the driver could see the red flag clearly again. By early afternoon the quarry ridge rose ahead.

desert_p10_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_068.text: Smoke from its receiving yard lay flat under the changing wind. The lower drainage hollow glimmered east of the road, farther from the wheel line than yesterday's worry had made it seem. Gao would compare current conditions at the shed and leave the new observations with the manager's clerk. Han would return the casks before calling the loan complete. Bao wanted news of the patient wagon. Tuo wanted a chair without wheels for the next rest. Each destination had become specific enough to prevent quarry from being merely another convenient name on the way home.

desert_p10_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_069.text: A little sand lizard crossed the road near the quarry bend, paused in a wheel shadow, and vanished beneath a rock before the team arrived. Yue almost pointed it out to Tuo, then saw the guide already watching. The creature had its own route through heat and shelter, unrelated to the subscribers' proposed loading ground. The basin's life kept appearing in these small timings. Grass rooted beneath salt; birds used glass in old windows; insects crossed a hollow slab. The land had never been empty simply because a map printed little there.

desert_p10_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_070.text: Yue followed the carts around the last quarry bend with that understanding awake. Before the next bend Yue saw fresh footprints leaving the public track toward a low stone shelter. They were human, two sizes, accompanied by a narrow dragging line that might belong to a bundle. No cart rut joined them. Tuo looked from her seat and asked the driver to pause at the wide shoulder. The shelter lay outside the dispatch route marked in the quarry book. A small strip of blue cloth moved at its entrance. Yue held the flag where the last cart could see.

desert_p10_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p10_071.text: The road had acquired another person-shaped question, and this time nobody had yet asked to be rescued.
